# Difference Matrix Method

A standard triad of summary statistics is the mean, median, and mode. The mean is a natural consequence of summations and moments. For the median and mode, the naive methods require branching logic, which we don't have. We introduce what we call the **difference matrix method** which will allow us to implement both statistics in a similar way (though still requiring tools from the [Discrete Math](/sign/intro.qmd) section, especially Equality and Max).

The tech tree below shows how the difference matrix method fits together, read from left to right. The basic moves build the difference matrix and sign. Sign gives equality and max, and the difference matrix and equality then combine into the median and the mode, with max also feeding the mode.

```{r}
#| label: dm-tech-tree
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.1
#| dev.args: !expr list(bg = "transparent")
#| fig-cap: "The tech tree for this section. The basic moves in the grey band build up to the difference matrix method, shown in bold orange."
#| fig-alt: "A flowchart read from left to right. A grey band labeled basic moves holds component-wise multiplication, addition, and cycle. All three feed into both the difference matrix and sign. Sign feeds into both equality and max. The difference matrix and equality both feed into median and mode, and max feeds into mode."

library(ggplot2)

boxes <- data.frame(
  label = c("Component-wise\nMultiplication", "Addition", "Cycle",
            "Difference\nMatrix", "Sign", "Equality", "Max", "Median", "Mode"),
  x = c(1.2, 1.2, 1.2, 3.8, 3.8, 5.8, 5.8, 7.8, 7.8),
  y = c(2.4, 1.2, 0, 1.2, 0, 0, -1.2, 1.2, 0),
  basic = c(TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, rep(FALSE, 6))
)
half_w <- ifelse(boxes$basic, 0.95, 0.72)
boxes$xmin <- boxes$x - half_w
boxes$xmax <- boxes$x + half_w
boxes$ymin <- boxes$y - 0.4
boxes$ymax <- boxes$y + 0.4

# Plain connector pieces, followed by the arrows that end at a box.
lines <- data.frame(
  x    = c(2.15, 2.15, 2.15, 2.5, 4.52, 4.8, 4.52, 6.52, 6.8, 6.52),
  xend = c(2.5, 2.5, 2.5, 2.5, 4.8, 4.8, 6.8, 6.8, 6.8, 7.8),
  y    = c(2.4, 1.2, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1.2, 0, 0, -1.2),
  yend = c(2.4, 1.2, 0, 2.4, 0, -1.2, 1.2, 0, 1.2, -1.2)
)
arrows <- data.frame(
  x    = c(2.5, 2.5, 4.8, 4.8, 6.8, 6.8, 7.8),
  xend = c(3.08, 3.08, 5.08, 5.08, 7.08, 7.08, 7.8),
  y    = c(1.2, 0, 0, -1.2, 1.2, 0, -1.2),
  yend = c(1.2, 0, 0, -1.2, 1.2, 0, -0.4)
)

neutral <- "grey50"
highlight <- "#E69F00"

ggplot() +
  annotate(
    "rect",
    xmin = 0.05, xmax = 2.35, ymin = -0.55, ymax = 2.95,
    fill = neutral, alpha = 0.12
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 1.2, y = -0.85, label = "Basic moves",
    color = neutral, size = 5, fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    data = lines,
    aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = yend),
    color = neutral, linewidth = 0.9
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    data = arrows,
    aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = yend),
    color = neutral, linewidth = 0.9,
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.1, "inches"), type = "closed")
  ) +
  geom_rect(
    data = boxes,
    aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax, color = basic),
    fill = NA, linewidth = 0.9
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = boxes[boxes$basic, ],
    aes(x = x, y = y, label = label),
    color = neutral, size = 4.2, fontface = "bold", lineheight = 0.9
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = boxes[!boxes$basic, ],
    aes(x = x, y = y, label = label),
    color = highlight, size = 5, fontface = "bold", lineheight = 0.9
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = neutral, `FALSE` = highlight), guide = "none") +
  coord_fixed(clip = "off") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA)
  )
```

The method is as follows:

Given a vector $z = (z_1, \ldots, z_{N/2})$, we construct an $(N/2) \times (N/2)$ matrix $D$ where $D_{i,j} = z_i - z_j$. We will call our matrix the **difference matrix.**

::: {.callout-tip icon="false" title="**Info**"}
**Remark**: our method is general enough that we should be able to compute $D$ where $D_{ij} = f(z_i, z_j)$ for some function $f$. We mention this but do not use the more general method in this work.
:::

Here is how we would generate the difference matrix:

1.  Assuming we are in the inter-vectors case, we can assume the $x_i$ are given as $u^{(i)} = (0, \ldots, 0, x_i, 0, \ldots, 0)$.

2.  We can "broadcast" the $x_i$ into every entry by computing $$v^{(i)} := \mathtt{sum}(u^{(i)}) = (x_i, \ldots, x_i).$$

3.  Now we can separately compute:

    -   $d_{i}=x-v^{(i)}=(x_1-x_i,x_2-x_i,\dots,x_{N/2}-x_i)$ for all $i$.
    -   If we wanted the transpose instead, we can compute:\
        $d'_{i}=v^{(i)}-x=(x_i-x_1, x_i-x_2,\dots, x_i-x_{N/2})$.

4.  We can think of the matrix as the combination of these vectors, though we might also want to isolate the use of our $N/2$ "difference vectors" of the form $$d_{i} = (d_{i,1}, \ldots, d_{i,N/2}).$$

::: {.callout-tip icon="false" title="**Info**"}
**Remark**: the above assumes the inter-vectors case. If we wanted the intra-vectors case, we can do something like the following:

1.  Given an input vector $(x_1, \ldots, x_{N/2})$,

2.  Define indicator vectors $c_i = (0,0,\dots,1_i,0\dots,0)$.

3.  Compute $x_i = \sum_{i=1}^{N/2}(c_i*x)$; this will isolate the $x$'s vector value at index $i$,

...and then the rest is the same as before.
:::
